question: Do the Bulacan PDPFP River Network and Wetlands Map or the PDRRMO Figure 3 provide enough spatial detail to verify the previously reviewed Angat River specimen's exact named reach?

data/research/philippines/national/revie.role: Prior occurrence-coordinate and modeled-reach plausibility review; source precision and exact reach remain unresolved.

provincialPlan.title: Bulacan Provincial Development and Physical Framework Plan 2024-2036, Draft Final Report
provincialPlan.map: Map 3.11, River Network and Wetlands Map
provincialPlan.visualReview: Province-wide raster page with satellite background, provincial/municipal context, coordinate graticules, generalized blue river-network lines, and wetland symbols. At this page scale the individual river/reach labels are not sufficiently legible to crosswalk the specimen point to a named channel segment.

provincialDisasterOffice.visualReview: Elevation-versus-distance profile, not a route map. The page text describes an approximately 61 km Angat River extent from Ipo Reservoir to the diversion in Labangan Channel; those endpoints and the profile do not supply a georeferenced centerline or a specimen-to-reach link.

method.coordinateHandling: The specimen's exact coordinate was not copied into this report, overlaid on the raster, or used to draw geometry. The prior review records that GBIF/BOLD did not supply coordinate uncertainty and that GBIF assumed WGS84.

findings.namedAngatSystemContext: The provincial plan shows a regional river-and-wetland network, while PDRRMO and PAGASA describe the Angat system and its downstream connection. These support water-system context only.
findings.sourceIndependence: The maps and hydrology descriptions do not independently identify the GBIF/BOLD/GenBank specimen or its collection reach.

rightsAndLimitations: The reviewed PDPFP map is embedded as a page image in a draft-final provincial plan. No item-specific reuse or redistribution license for its map artwork was identified; the local source copy remains Git-ignored.
The PDRRMO Figure 3 profile is dated January 2006 and is a longitudinal profile, not a geospatial route layer.
Province-wide visual context and named system descriptions cannot resolve source coordinate uncertainty, current reach geometry, present-day fish presence, catchability, access, or safety.

decision.disposition: Retain the historical record as a previously reviewed Angat River source-chain candidate. The official provincial map and longitudinal profile do not resolve its exact named reach; do not map the occurrence or generate a river line from these pages.

nextAction: Continue Central Luzon evidence work with independent site-resolved fish surveys, specimen records, or reusable geospatial river sources; do not recount the BPC001-13/ANAd1 chain as new evidence.
